root_idea.summary: The root denotes force, hardness, and strength, especially force exerted in handling or moving something.
root_idea.development: The semantic range develops from heavy, strong implements and physical force to forcibly drawing or dragging, and further to descriptions of rough, harsh, or coarse character.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic imperative is normalized to the Form I perfect citation form عَتَلَ.
The inflected Quranic adjective is displayed under the normalized citation form عُتُلّ.

senses.definition: To seize hold of someone, push or thrust him, and drag or drive him away roughly and violently.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction takes an object and directs it toward a destination; the forceful manner is integral. In the supplied occurrence, the destination is the middle of Hell.

senses.definition: A voracious, withholding person who roughly takes or drags things to himself.
senses.usage_conditions: One explanation of the Quranic occurrence in 68:13 centers on excessive eating, refusal to give, and rough handling.

senses.definition: A gross, coarse, harsh, churlish, or cruel person, low or mean in disposition, vehement in quarrel, resistant to admonition, or unwilling to be led toward good.
senses.usage_conditions: Another Quran-attested explanation of the occurrence in 68:13 emphasizes harsh character and resistance to correction or goodness rather than appetite.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lead a she-camel roughly or violently by taking hold of its nose-rein.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction عَتَلَ النَّاقَةَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or be quick to do evil or mischief.
A man who hastens or is quick to do evil or mischief.
Mutual pushing or thrusting, roughly or violently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the reciprocal Form III verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be drawn or dragged roughly or violently, or to submit to being led.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or passive-like Form VII usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave one's place or come along with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional usage in the expression لا أَنْعَتِلُ مَعَكَ, literally used in the negative for refusing to go along.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A carpenter's auger, wimble, or gimlet.
An iron implement for pulling up or cutting young palm shoots, palm branches, or grape-vine shoots.
A broad-headed iron tool for digging or excavating earth and walls, or for demolishing walls.
A thick wooden staff, including a shoulder-pole used by two men to carry burdens.
A Persian bow or a strong bow.
A large clod of clay or cohesive earth pulled from the ground during ploughing.
A she-camel that does not conceive and is consequently always strong.
Gross, coarse, rough, and strong in bodily constitution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or beast, and according to some authorities to anything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thick spear.
A hard mountain.
A hired man, hireling, or servant.
A violent or severe disease or malady.
A porter or carrier of burdens for hire, using a shoulder-pole.
An aide or officer of the prefect of the police.
Strong in drawing or dragging something roughly or violently.

cautions: The Quranic adjective عُتُلّ in 68:13 has several closely related classical explanations, including appetite and withholding, rough handling, and harsh or coarse character; the two numbered senses preserve these materially distinct interpretive branches.
The Quranic verb is attested in an imperative inflection, but the public headword is the normalized Form I perfect citation form عَتَلَ.
